reviewer.method: Round-5 (v10) independent pass, performed from scratch rather than as a diff against findings-preview-v9.json. Scope: the four new elements this revision round added to scenes 1-4 (music-staff prop + 'partitur latihan' label in shot-0; subtle mv() zoom-in on the vidka-aha portrait in shot-4; filter-chip search-refinement line in the zoomed search-box shot; 'tinjauan pustaka' corner tag in the source-labeling hold shot), plus a full re-check of all 7 B1 criteria across all 14 sample shots (shot-0 through shot-13). Method: read output/preview-reference/evidence.json's plan.shots directly for ground-truth shot boundaries (confirmed byte-identical to v9's: shot-0 0-2.838, shot-1 2.838-5.677, shot-2 5.677-9.461, shot-3 9.461-11.123, shot-4 11.123-15.0, shot-5 15.0-17.821, shot-6 17.821-24.403, shot-7 24.403-30.0, shot-8 30.0-33.564, shot-9 33.564-40.183, shot-10 40.183-45.183, shot-11 45.183-48.015, shot-12 48.015-54.623, shot-13 54.623-60.0 -- scene 1's SCENE_MIN floor of 15.0s total and every internal cut inside it are unchanged from the last approved v9 pass, so every v9 observation time remains in-range and no stale-timestamp issue exists this round). Read project.json's full shot layer list (42,[shots 0-13] correspond 1:1 to metadata.scenes[0..13] and to evidence.json's shot-0..shot-13) to get exact coordinates, 'from'/'to' gating and mv() keyframes for every layer, then independently extracted targeted frames from the current output/preview.mp4 with ffmpeg (not reused stale crops) at each new element's relevant times, at upscaled crops where sub-pixel placement mattered, to visually confirm what the coordinates implied. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the task brief handed to me: cross-checking project.json against evidence.json's shot index mapping shows the filter-chip text '"musik" · jurnal terindeks · 2020–2026' (x=160,y=70,size=28,from=1.128) is NOT in shot-5 as the brief stated -- it is in shot-5's own project.json record is the unchanged wide laptop shot (metadata scene=2 shot=1, 15.0-17.821s, label 'Pencarian literatur akademik', unaffected this round); the new filter-chip line is in shot-6 (metadata scene=2 shot=2, 17.821-24.403s, the zoomed search-box close-up), confirmed by grepping project.json's shots array index 6 for the literal string and cross-referencing metadata.scenes[6]. Consequently the brief's claim that shot-5 'shares' this text with 'Pencarian literatur akademik' is also incorrect -- those two labels are in different, non-overlapping shots (shot-5 ends at 17.821s, shot-6 begins there) and never co-occur on screen, so there is no crowding question to resolve between them; I checked shot-5 and shot-6 each on their own merits instead. All four target elements were independently confirmed present, correctly placed and defect-free; no blocking issue was found in any of the 14 shots. Carried-forward content (shots 1,2,3,5,7,8,9,11,12,13, none of which this round's edits touch) was not rubber-stamped: for each I either re-extracted a fresh frame from the current preview.mp4 or read the already-current output/preview-reference/shot-N-*.png (generated from this exact preview.mp4, sha256 3d0391b2... per evidence.json, at 2026-11-25 08:02, i.e. not stale) and visually compared it against project.json's layer data and against the v9 prose before writing each observation in my own words below; where v9's description matched what I independently saw I say so, and I did not change any wording that referenced the old mistimed (v7/v8) schedule because v9 had already corrected all of that and the schedule has not moved again since.

An 8-frame tile across 13.5-14.95s shows a smooth, continuous push-in with no pop, no clipping of Vidka's figure against the frame edges (closest edge distance at full zoom: right edge 1280-1191=89px), and nothing drifting in an unintended direction.
